findings.title: Observe immediate sampler validation before publishing Ok
findings.scenario: On WgpuContext::new_compute() or new() native owned context with no surrounding external validation scope, call Sampler::new with Some(SamplerAddressMode::ClampToBorder) on any address axis. The enum is publicly admitted directly, through serde/strum, or numeric 3.0 conversion. Owned context descriptor requests only FLOAT32_FILTERABLE, FLOAT32_BLENDABLE and TIMESTAMP_QUERY, so ADDRESS_MODE_CLAMP_TO_BORDER is absent regardless of adapter support.
findings.effect: wgpu-core rejects at create_sampler immediately. Backend error routing reaches default uncaptured handler and panics before Result can return; a custom handler instead permits publication of an invalid sampler as Ok. This is source-proven public API behavior, not a runtime observation and not a claim of current internal ClampToBorder use.
findings.minimum_connected_repair: Root must inventory all thirteen lenses before edit; use existing immediate context.observe_validation around create_sampler, propagate actual native cause through current anyhow result before Arc/Ok publication. No new feature request, default/filter/address policy, poll/wait, alias/device metadata or compatibility path. Preserve borrowed/browser device-handled policy.
findings.consumer_effect: Only actual internal wrapper constructor call observed is GpuMesh::displacement, gpu.rs:231, all options None (Repeat/Linear defaults), with ? propagation and PassParameter insertion. Advect::execute accepts but does not use its sampler argument. Static sampler binding rejects missing native handle and enclosing group scope observes native incompatibility; reflection sampler declarations remain unchanged.
